artifact_observation.command: nm -u on the already-existing object (read-only inspection)
artifact_observation.result: Only PMPI lifecycle imports are _pmpi_init_ and _pmpi_finalize_; no MPI state/thread query imports. The object has a 32-bit MPI_Fint/int static assertion. This is compile/link-symbol evidence only, not a full WRF or MPI runtime validation.

checks.evidence: The phase hook calls are guarded by WRF_NATIVE_EXIT_TRACE. test_native_exit_trace.py pins the default-off preprocessed output hashes for all three authoritative Fortran sources against merged PR #317.

C observer records init/finalize entry/return and phase markers; mpi_init_ and mpi_finalize_ each forward once to the matching PMPI symbol using the original ierr pointer and record the PMPI-written value. Static source inspection found no extra MPI lifecycle calls, state queries, or status mutation. Existing fake-PMPI tests reportedly passed.

Recorder uses a new session for its owned direct child, records/waits through that Popen handle, forwards one SIGINT only to the direct child after KeyboardInterrupt, reports direct-child return status, and makes no process-group-emptiness claim. Existing non-MPI child tests reportedly passed.

Guide distinguishes MPI_THREAD_SINGLE from MPI_THREAD_FUNNELED and says the observer does not query/certify thread support. It labels C CLOCK_MONOTONIC and Python monotonic/wall samples as separate domains and limits timestamp claims to sampled request/event times.

Guide requires a separately built and pinned diagnostic executable/object, explains frozen-binding incompatibility, treats launcher RC 0 as launcher-only, and explicitly leaves full WRF rebuild/deployment validation open. Existing extracted-Fortran call-order test reportedly passed.

final_delta_review.canonical_validation_pins: validation.json now pins the current C observer, test, recorder, Fortran hooks, and workflow hashes. The raw test log is pinned and records five tests passing (exit 0); actual Open MPI header compile is recorded without external POSIX define and with no MPI runtime invocation.
final_delta_review.delta: The guarded _POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809L definition is the first source content, before headers; it does not override an existing definition and contains no logic change.
final_delta_review.historical_checklist: C1-C5 and C2a are marked done/resolved; R1 remains open for the unknown historical two-launcher-RC1 cause.
final_delta_review.scope: Static check only; no tests or launches rerun.
final_delta_review.self_contained_test_flags: Current fake_objects() C11 flags contain no -D_POSIX_C_SOURCE. The observer itself provides the feature-test macro before all headers.

historical_finding.statement: Historical two-launcher-RC1 cause remains unknown and is not attributed to the new hooks or trace.

limitations: All five tests are reported by the root agent as passing; they were not rerun during this final review.
No WRF rebuild, executable launch, actual MPI finalization under the new observer, deployment run, or scientific validation has been performed for these new hooks.
The standalone recorder waits for its direct launcher child and does not independently prove that all descendants or ranks have exited; the guide explicitly disclaims that inference.
Existing native case completion and the historical cause of the two launcher RC1 outcomes remain separate questions.

The refreshed validation artifacts pin the final C observer and test hashes; five local non-MPI tests and the Open MPI header-only object compile are recorded, but no full WRF build or MPI runtime execution of the new hooks was performed.
